elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 3.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ... for convenience by: a. providing at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to IBM". Service Option Attachments are the Order-Form-selected attachments, so both agreement-level and order-level exit are covered. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a pattern artifact (the phrase "for convenience" is separated from the notice words by the parenthetical and the "by:" list); on substance the right is expressly present.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Notice reduced from "at least one month's prior written notice" to "at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to IBM", and the effectiveness anchor "at the end of any calendar month" is deleted, so termination is no longer deferred past the 30-day period.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "IBM will refund prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination on a pro-rata basis." This is an express pro-rata basis, not merely a post-termination-period refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only exits in the cited provisions are material breach (3.3) and the Section 3.2 auto-renewal notice, which must be given "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term" and terminates the Attachment at the end of that term \u2014 natural-term non-renewal assessed under RENEWAL, not mid-term T4C. No mid-term Vendor convenience right is retained or created.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered notice is thirty (30) days, outside the 60\u201390 day band (this is deliberate, as the drafter targets the preferred level).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No cap is inserted; the Attachment A early termination charges (and the retained subparagraph b of Section 3.4) remain uncapped. The rationale expressly reserves this point rather than drafting it.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 3.2 notice operates only "prior to the end of the then-current term" and terminates the Attachment at that term end; no mid-term IBM convenience right exists.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 3.2 requires written notice "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term".

reasons: Preferred level is complete: Customer convenience right over the Agreement and any Service Option Attachment, 30 days' notice with the calendar-month-end anchor removed, an express pro-rata refund of prepaid charges, and no retained IBM mid-term convenience right.
Fallback is incomplete (30-day notice is outside the 60\u201390 band and no three-month early-termination fee cap is drafted), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is fully met.

Minimality holds: the edits are confined to the notice period, the month-end effectiveness anchor (which would otherwise defeat the 30-day element), and a one-sentence refund insertion. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories, or boilerplate was added; the retained subparagraph b, the IBM continuing-performance sentence, and the Section 3.2 renewal mechanic are untouched.

Intent is preserved: the prerequisite-Attachment carve-out, IBM's duty to keep performing to the final termination date, the Section 3.5 accrued-charge acceleration, and the Attachment A charge mechanics all survive without contradiction \u2014 a refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period does not conflict with payment of charges already accrued.

Deterministic flag "Customer convenience termination present: false" was inspected in substance and is a regex adjacency artifact, not a drafting defect; the operative sentence grants the right expressly.

Deviation status is correct for the original clause (no prepaid-charge refund, and effectiveness deferred to calendar month-end), though the original already gave a fairly short customer exit, so the residual harm is modest.
